key_insight: Replacing abstract language prompts with explicit points of physical contact yields more physically grounded and reliable robot utility models. Contact-Anchored Policies (CAP) use contact locations as conditioning signals to produce modular, robust manipulation behaviors.
problem_solved: Language conditioning is often too abstract to convey the concrete physical information required for robust robotic manipulation; CAP addresses the gap between high-level instructions and low-level contact-rich control.
method: Condition policies on explicit 3D contact points in the environment instead of natural language prompts.
Structure the approach as a library of modular utility models (CAP modules) anchored to contact locations to enable compositional reuse across tasks and embodiments.
Use contact-conditioned utilities to select and compose low-level actions for contact-rich manipulation, improving physical grounding and task reliability.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, CAP offers a practical alternative to language-conditioned controllers by providing clearer, physically meaningful conditioning signals that improve generalization and modular reuse in manipulation tasks.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison: language-conditioned pipeline vs contact-anchored pipeline (showing how contact points directly influence action selection).

paper_title: Contact-Anchored Policies: Contact Conditioning Creates Strong Robot Utility Models
paper_authors: Zichen Jeff Cui, Omar Rayyan, Haritheja Etukuru, Bowen Tan, Zavier Andrianarivo
